claims.text: Ab initio calculations can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio calculations can be used to tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The relevant mediator for tuning is the compositional space of high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio calculations enable tuning by predicting alloy behavior under various conditions.
Computational prediction can identify potential non-equiatomic HEA candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
There is currently no method for tuning magnetic and magnetocaloric properties in the stated context.
Computational methods have limitations in predicting experimental outcomes.
The accuracy of ab initio predictions for the behavior of high-entropy alloys is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that there is currently no tuning method, whereas the hypothesis identifies ab initio calculations as such a method. This could represent a pre-intervention baseline, but that temporal distinction is not stated.
